newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar closes flat in busy trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar closes flat in busy trading.

text.p: * Canada's dollar closed almost flat on Thursday at C$1.3668 (US$0.7317), despite weakening overnight on selling in Asia and London, dealers said.
* They said the currency recovered on solid retail sales numbers, stronger bonds and a surging stock market in fairly heavy volume.
The statistic was much stronger than economists' projections.

Trade numbers for October released on Thursday were lower than expected but the decline was due mainly to a three-week strike at General Motors Corp's Canada unit. The currency market ignored the number and focused on retail sales instead, dealers said.

Strong stocks and bonds also helped the Canadian unit gain strength during the day, dealers said. The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 index rose 116.66 points to 5,844.30, the third biggest net gain for the index.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$2.00 to C$110.55 to yield 7.109 percent.
Dealers said the currency is expected to move slightly stronger again on Friday.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 1.1388 marks from Wednesday's close of 1.1348 marks and edged up to 83.38 yen from 83.19 yen.
